patterns_data.top_pattern: CT PPO residential behavioral health is rising through higher volume and higher paid per case
patterns_data.what_is_impacting: CT Commercial Individual PPO residential behavioral health treatment
key_driver_codes: Alcohol, Drug Abuse or Dependence without Rehabilitation Therapy without MCC
patterns_data.pattern_details: CT PPO spending increased sharply across residential behavioral health settings, with the larger rise in RESIDENTIAL TREATMENT CTR and a smaller but still material increase in RESIDENTIAL TREATMENT FACILITY. Both more episodes and higher paid per case are contributing, so this is not just a volume issue or just a price issue. The pattern is concentrated in substance-use treatment, making it a focused site-of-care and reimbursement opportunity.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: This is one of the largest operational cost levers and requires coordinated authorization, level-of-care, and reimbursement action in CT PPO behavioral health.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Run a CT PPO residential behavioral health action plan that combines prior authorization and level-of-care review with rate and contract review for residential treatment settings.
evidence_summary: CT PPO residential treatment spending rose +$3.1M across RESIDENTIAL TREATMENT CTR and RESIDENTIAL TREATMENT FACILITY.
The largest driver added +$2.6M with +221 claims and about +$5.5K higher paid per case at RESIDENTIAL TREATMENT CTR.
RESIDENTIAL TREATMENT FACILITY added +$455K with +25 claims and about +$18.2K higher paid per case.
The same substance-use DRG is driving both settings, pointing to a focused behavioral health site-of-care issue.

patterns_data.top_pattern: CT inpatient behavioral health growth is concentrated in substance-use diagnoses
patterns_data.what_is_impacting: CT inpatient behavioral health for substance-use admissions
key_driver_codes: Alcohol and Drug Abuse Treatment Services
patterns_data.pattern_details: CT inpatient behavioral health growth is concentrated in a narrow set of substance-use diagnoses rather than a broad all-category increase. Most of the increase reflects both more claims and higher paid per case, and several of the newer high-cost episodes show blank procedure coding. This points to a targeted substance-use management issue with a parallel coding cleanup need.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: Targeted action on these diagnoses can reduce spend without broad behavioral health policy changes.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Launch focused inpatient behavioral health review for CT substance-use admissions, including medical necessity and level-of-care review, and validate blank procedure coding on the higher-cost cases.
patterns_data.validation_reason: Several CT inpatient behavioral health drivers include Null or Blank procedure coding, so claim classification should be checked alongside clinical intervention.
evidence_summary: CT IP BH case-mix growth totaled +$3.2M across related substance-use diagnosis groups.
F1020 with Alcohol and Drug Abuse Treatment Services added +$686K on +98 claims, and F10239 added +$560K on +71 claims.
Rare higher-cost episodes added another +$681K, including +$383K for F1520 and +$298K for F1120 with blank procedure coding.
Across the main drivers, paid per case increased by roughly $2.5K to $9.9K.

patterns_data.top_pattern: Not Mapped and UNATTRIBUTED records are a gating validation issue across outpatient and specialty services
patterns_data.what_is_impacting: Outpatient specialty drugs, supplies, lab, and miscellaneous services with Not Mapped or UNATTRIBUTED classification
patterns_data.pattern_details: A meaningful share of the increase sits in Not Mapped or UNATTRIBUTED buckets across multiple segments and service types. Because facility, state, or service classification is unclear, these records should not drive authorization tightening or reimbursement changes until mapping is corrected. This is a gating data and coding issue that affects the reliability of downstream UM, network, and clinical decisions.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: If the mapping is wrong, the business can take the wrong action on provider performance, site of care, or authorization policy.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Run a focused data-quality audit on Not Mapped and UNATTRIBUTED records for facility type, state attribution, DRG classification, and outpatient drug or lab categorization, then rerun impacted utilization and reimbursement decisions after correction.
patterns_data.validation_reason: The evidence includes repeated Not Mapped and UNATTRIBUTED classifications, low-volume specialty records, and provider-specific outpatient activity that may be misclassified.
evidence_summary: Not Mapped or UNATTRIBUTED records drove about +$1.4M across UNATTRIBUTED, ME, CA / CO, CO, CA, GA, and IN.
The largest item was UNATTRIBUTED OP Mgmt Oth Misc D66 drugs at +$679K from 2 claims, tagged Not Mapped.
ME PPO Not Mapped operational spend added +$513K on +119 claims, while CA / CO outpatient specialty drug and supply activity added about +$98K.
GA lab and operational Not Mapped activity added small dollars but high claim counts at THREE RIVERS DIAGNOSTICS, which looks more like classification risk than a core cost trend.

patterns_data.top_pattern: ME facility spending is being pushed by acute hospital pricing and smaller rehab growth
patterns_data.what_is_impacting: ME acute hospital HMO and physical rehab PPO facility spend
patterns_data.pattern_details: ME shows two facility cost issues with different profiles. The larger issue is an acute hospital HMO price spike on a very small base, while the smaller PPO physical rehab increase reflects both more claims and higher paid per case. The business response should separate claim-level pricing validation from broader contract and utilization action.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: ME facility trend can be overstated by a single high-cost acute event unless pricing is validated before broader network action.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Validate the high-cost acute hospital HMO claim at the claim-pricing level first, then review PPO physical rehab reimbursement and utilization controls as a second action.
patterns_data.validation_reason: The acute hospital component is a small-base unit-cost spike with no claim growth, so repricing validation is needed before treating it as a contract trend.
evidence_summary: ME facility cost pressure totaled +$643K across HMO acute hospital and PPO physical rehab.
Acute hospital HMO contributed +$485K with no claim growth, indicating pure unit cost pressure on a very small base.
PPO physical rehab added +$158K on +99 claims with about +$1.5K higher paid per case.

patterns_data.pattern_details: TX HMO non-residential behavioral health spending rose because more services were used, not because price increased. patterns_data.why_it_matters: When volume is the main driver, authorization and care-navigation changes are more likely to work than rate action.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Review prior authorization criteria, referral patterns, and level-of-care management for TX HMO non-residential behavioral health to reduce avoidable volume.
evidence_summary: TX HMO NON RESIDENTIAL spending grew +$514K.
The increase was volume-led with +184 claims while paid per case fell about $4.1K.
The same substance-use DRG concentrated the change, pointing to more episodes rather than price escalation.

key_driver_codes: Esophagitis, Gastroenteritis and Miscellaneous Digestive Disorders without MCC
patterns_data.pattern_details: Rare inpatient Med/Surg outliers in IN / UNATTRIBUTED are dominated by one liver transplant case and one additional digestive disorder admission. These cases have almost no volume but very high spend, so they should be handled as claim-level catastrophic outliers rather than a broad inpatient trend. The financial effect is material even though the episode count is minimal.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: Single catastrophic admissions can distort trend and require a different response than standard utilization or pricing issues.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Perform claim-level clinical, stop-loss, and reimbursement validation on the transplant and other outlier admissions before taking any broader inpatient action.
patterns_data.validation_reason: This pattern is driven by one-claim events with low baseline volume, so claim-level validation is needed before extrapolating.
evidence_summary: IN / UNATTRIBUTED IP Med/Surg rare outliers totaled +$505K.
A single Liver Transplant without MCC case drove +$486K.
A separate digestive disorder case at IU HEALTH BALL MEMORIAL HOSPITAL added +$19K.
